title: "Graph Algorithms and Connectivity"
description: "A connected learning path through 7 worked algorithms topics."

## What you are really learning

Turn relationships into vertices/edges and make correctness depend on reachability, order or weights.

The goal is not to learn 7 unrelated definitions. Compare the operations needed by each classic problem and notice which invariant survives from one technique to the next.

## Begin with a small example

A cheaper route can use more edges.

$$
d(C)=\min(5,2+1)=3
$$

**What the symbols mean:** d(C) is minimum cost to city C from source A; direct A→C costs 5; the alternative A→B and B→C costs 2 plus 1.

**Substitute actual numbers:** The two-hop route costs 3, which is smaller than direct cost 5. This is why a weighted shortest path problem is not merely BFS.

This is how the topic pages below should be read: understand the numbers first, then generalise to the equation.

## The chapters in this family

1. **[Union-Find](../union-find/index.qmd)** — Maintain disjoint equivalence classes as edges or unions arrive.
2. **[Shortest Path](../shortest-path/index.qmd)** — Minimise a path's total edge weight between vertices.
3. **[Topological Sort](../topological-sort/index.qmd)** — Order a directed acyclic graph so dependencies precede consumers.
4. **[Minimum Spanning Tree](../minimum-spanning-tree/index.qmd)** — Connect all vertices with minimum total edge cost and no cycle.
5. **[Strongly Connected Component](../strongly-connected-component/index.qmd)** — Partition a directed graph by mutual reachability.
6. **[Biconnected Component](../biconnected-component/index.qmd)** — Identify undirected graph blocks that cannot be disconnected by one internal articulation vertex.
7. **[Eulerian Circuit](../eulerian-circuit/index.qmd)** — Traverse every edge exactly once and return to the starting vertex.

## Practice method

Choose ONE chapter. Reproduce its example with paper and pencil, identify what is cached or discarded, implement the tiny idea, and explain one case in which the algorithm's assumptions fail. Repeat until the invariant feels natural.

The [original executable examples](../examples/README.md) provide code you can run and test. If two topics seem similar, compare them in the [algorithm selection guide](../guides/choose-a-pattern.qmd).
